items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: Luis Russell used to work with us, with me in New Orleans with Paul Barbarin and Willie Santiago

ctx.x: I can't remember because I left Oliver in about '25, I think it was. And we went to -- No, we came to New York. That's when I left Oliver.

We played the Savoy Ballroom and we had a battle with Chick Webb and Fletcher Henderson. And they wanted to hire Oliver at the Savoy for about four or five weeks but they didn't want to give him the money that he wanted. So we didn't have a job and we didn't have anything else to do. So then I got -- Luis Russell used to work with us, with me in New Orleans with Paul Barbarin and Willie Santiago and a trumpet player named Arnold Matwire.

items.title: Barney Bigard Interview, 1969-07-25
items.q: Right. It was Albert Nicholas and Paul Barberin.

ctx.x: Hi Bill, this is Floyd Levin in Los Angeles. This is the 25th of July 1969 and shortly I expect Barney Begard over, at which time I will supply the questions and hopefully he'll come up with some of the answers to help you on your quest for information about Jelly Roll Morton. Okay, we've just played the Victor Trio session, Barney. I assume that you have some memories about that session. Yeah, I was really surprised. I thought I played more than I do now. That's going back, what, 40 years? Yes, it is. Could you…
. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. That's okay. You can cut that off. One. Two. You see, if you count and then pick back the notes up, it screws you up. Yeah. ¶ Thank you.

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1960-01-28
items.q: Well, he took the clarinet while we were working at Tom Anderson. He and Albert Nicholas team were together.

ctx.x: When did he take up the clarinet?

Well, he took the clarinet while we were working at Tom Anderson. He and Albert Nicholas team were together. He played like a flute at that time. He used to call him Snake Chalmers. He used to call him. He used to kill him all the time. Albert Nicholas used to laugh at him all the time. So I told him, don't pay attention about laughing at him. Just continue trying to play his horn. Keep on practicing. Well, that guy came up very fast. When he was in King Oliver's band, he started featuring the clarinet. He…
Did he ever play clarinet at all with Oliver?
